research_question: Among 904 candidate rice lines, which single line has the highest measured 100-grain weight (GRWT100)?

input_data.selection_rule: top-20 by E1 predicted GRWT100 (argmax-probability under a Gaussian error model is monotone in prediction, so the top-20 predicted set maximizes P(true argmax measured within budget))

control_variables: same historical source panel as the model training data family.
execution_evidence: 20 separate query_evidence_oracle(candidate_id=...) calls, one per top-20 predicted line, returning {"candidate_id","measurement","evidence_type":"E3"}. No UNOBSERVABLE returned; oracle budget exhausted (20/20). Query order: IRIS_313.12254, .12242, .12344, .12228, .11094, .11623, .12063, .12352, .12262, .12342, .10679, .12321, .12134, .12349, .12129, .10653, .12227, .10660, .11845, .12330.
uncertainty: All 20 queried lines came from one tail of the prediction distribution; the panel-level trait mean and sd are not directly observed. The 0.3 g margin of the top line over the runner-up exceeds the expected rounding error (0.05 g) but not the model's residual sd (~0.47 g).
conclusion: Real historical GRWT100 measurements for the 20 top-predicted lines. The highest measured value is IRIS_313.12254 = 5.0 g, which is also the model's rank-1 prediction. Runner-up IRIS_313.12349 = 4.7 g (model rank 14). Measured values range 2.8-5.0 (mean 3.61, sd 0.62). Rank agreement with prediction is positive (Spearman 0.473), so H1 is supported on both of its falsification clauses.
limitations: Only 20 of 904 lines measured, all from the extreme upper tail of predictions -> truncated sample

the calibration slope and residual sd estimated from these 20 are therefore uncertain and the relationship cannot be checked in the mid/lower range. Values are single-environment historical records with no replication estimate. One measurement per line
no independent remeasurement possible within budget.

research_question: Given only 20 measurements among 904 candidates, how likely is it that an unmeasured candidate exceeds the observed maximum GRWT100 of 5.0 g?
control_variables: threshold fixed at the observed max 5.0 g
calibration parameters integrated over sampling error.
execution_evidence: Derived computation on ev-1 (E1 predictions) + ev-2 (E3 measurements): analysis/analyze.py and analysis/sensitivity.py in the run directory; OLS calibration, Monte Carlo over the (a,b) covariance (20,000 draws) and chi-square noise draws, plus a residual-sd sensitivity grid.
uncertainty: P(no exceed) reported as a range 0.93-1.00 driven mainly by residual-sd uncertainty; the point estimate from the 20 analysed pairs is 0.998.
conclusion: Calibration of E1 predictions to E3 measurements: measured = -8.10 + 3.49*pred (slope t=3.94), residual sd 0.465 g. Under this model the 884 unqueried lines have expected count above 5.0 g of ~0.00-0.08 and P(no unqueried line exceeds the observed 5.0 g) = 0.94-1.00, depending on the residual-sd assumption (0.47 -> ~1.00; 0.60 -> 0.997; 0.80 -> 0.93). The top risk unqueried line is IRIS_313.11705 (pred 3.171).
limitations: Calibration is extrapolated from a truncated (top-20 only) sample, so the slope and especially the residual sd are estimated over a narrow prediction range (3.17-3.66). Gaussian error and residual independence are assumptions
heavy tails or heteroscedasticity would raise the risk. Panel mean/sd of GRWT100 are not observed. The probability is therefore a model-based statement (E2), not a measured fact.
